findings.title: The texture layout was not linear
findings.found: The first full-width texture interpretation was wrong. Recovered upload traversal established tiled storage instead.
findings.why: A file can pass size checks while its pixels are decoded in the wrong order. The decoder was corrected.
findings.unknown: These are custom repacked structures, not ordinary TIM files or universal texture coverage.

findings.title: The pose packing is mapped
findings.found: Bit-origin reconstruction recovered sparse axes and an overlapping-store effect in one packed pose helper.
findings.why: There is a testable mapping behind the pose decoder, not just a plausible-looking model.
findings.unknown: A fixed-block check, not a complete animation system or provenance clearance.

findings.title: Sequence calls are not frames
findings.found: The primary updater was checked against a separate oracle. A zero duration expires after 256 update calls.
findings.why: A repeating hold is not an end signal. Assuming a frame rate would change the animation semantics.
findings.unknown: 55 nonempty sequences are exposed; timing and a complete animation system are not established.

findings.title: Geometry is real; gameplay is not
findings.found: A bounded environment decoder matched 863 reference rows, retaining coordinates, UVs, flags and material evidence.
findings.why: The scene has structured reconstruction evidence beyond an isolated visual guess.
findings.unknown: Visibility, broader orientations, collision and material semantics remain incomplete.

findings.title: A character is more than loose parts
findings.found: Recovered hierarchy and part mapping support a diagnostic character with 317 vertices and 316 faces.
findings.why: Part identities connect to a skeleton; duplicate render packets were workspaces, not extra faces.
findings.unknown: Transforms are approximate. Full animation and original GPU/GTE fidelity are not established.

findings.title: The first inspected map is not boot
findings.found: The zero-state startup path resolves to ST01. Its established direct order is INIT_DAT → DEMO_DAT → ST01.
findings.why: The earlier ST1C environment cannot be substituted for the first startup scene or called a title screen.
findings.unknown: This is not the complete dependency set, an executed native scene or a boot result.

findings.title: Native policy is not BIOS equivalence
findings.found: Selected A0:39 analysis reports five ordered word stores. The accepted native heap policy deliberately preserves guest RAM.
findings.why: A passing native-policy test does not prove the original firmware performed the same effects.
findings.unknown: Actual game-time dispatch, allocator invariants and inherited GPU state remain unresolved.

findings.title: Observe without inventing a step
findings.found: A four-case envelope captured bounded owner state, including the actual pending A0:49 request.
findings.why: Inspection can report where execution stopped without pretending the pending service completed.
findings.unknown: Fingerprints are not full-state introspection. No Windows capture or live-debugger acceptance.

findings.title: Old data is allowed to look old
findings.found: Delayed wakes recover sampled data; failed observations retain explicit stale/as-of labels without replaying requests.
findings.why: An old snapshot must never silently masquerade as current runtime state.
findings.unknown: Mode repetitions are not unique tests. No timing guarantee, LeakSanitizer pass or native-owner retirement.

findings.title: The original game reached story
findings.found: An author-reported emulator capture progressed past loading into the opening story, with observed entry and caller boundaries.
findings.why: This is executed reference research, not merely a catalog of manuals or a static hypothesis.
findings.unknown: Not native-port boot, physical-console proof, complete gameplay or implementation clearance.

findings.title: A0:49 is not a safe no-op
findings.found: Research observed GPU-access callbacks before a context-matched caller return; access payloads remain unknown.
findings.why: Ignoring a return value does not mean the call had no effects. A success constant would invent state.
findings.unknown: Effective dispatch, full ABI, GPU history and current native binding remain open.

findings.title: Cancel requested ≠ work retired
findings.found: New load and host-I/O reviews separate cancellation intent, actual completion, resource settlement and execution retirement.
findings.why: A timeout or an overlapped handle cannot be relabeled as a safe, bounded shutdown.
findings.unknown: No admitted production backend, controller implementation or new Windows test. L1/P1 remain unmet.

provenance: Private evidence is summarized and not independently reproducible here. PSX-SPX remains a restricted-provenance research reference, not cleared implementation authority.
